objective: Make the ApexYard gates run inside Codex after a guided one-time trust step per user, warn when trust is missing or stale, block Codex apply_patch edits the same way as Claude edits, remove the hook-trust bypass flag from all guidance, and prove the Edit-matcher hooks give the same decisions when Codex runs them in parallel.
why: ac3-1 ac3-2 and ac3-4 are not-verified and ac3-3 is partially-verified. Codex skips untrusted hooks without a warning, so Codex builds may run with no gates today. Managed hooks need a machine-wide sudo install, so the operator chose per-user trust only. Codex passes apply_patch with tool_name apply_patch and only the patch text, and with no file_path require-active-ticket.sh line 302 allows the call, so the ticket-first gate fails open on patches. Codex runs matching hooks in parallel.

include: A setup step that walks the user through the Codex hook trust step for the generated hooks
A check that warns when the ApexYard hooks are untrusted or their trust is stale after a hook change
Verify that the CI path that seeds ~/.codex at the pinned Codex version still gets trusted hooks and record the result
An apply_patch shim in the Codex adapter that extracts every Add and Update and Delete and Move path from the patch and blocks when any path blocks
A test that a Codex patch touching a code path without an active ticket is blocked and a docs-only patch is allowed
Replace --dangerously-bypass-hook-trust in docs/harnesses/codex.md and docs/harnesses/README.md and both setup and handover skill copies and docs/spike-848/findings.md with the per-user trust step
A test that runs the Edit-matcher hooks in parallel many times and in order and compares the decisions
exclude: A machine-wide or sudo install of Codex managed hooks
Changes to the Claude Code hook path
